name: EQ layered synths: carve shared frequency space
goal: Fit stacked hook synths/pads/strings without mud: high-pass non-bass layers (~below 100 Hz consistently), use bell cuts to carve competing mid buildups, optionally commit drastic low cuts on bright toppers (e.g. below 1 kHz) so they sit as air/presence, and ease harsh upper bands by ear—giving each layer its own spectrum.

source.title: How to EQ Layered Synths in a Mix

prerequisites: Multiple layered synth/pad/string tracks; parametric EQ

outputs.name: eqd_synth_stack
outputs.description: Layered synths with complementary EQ carves

steps.action: Solo the layered hook synths/strings (without bass) and note masking/mud before EQ.
steps.expect: Hear overlap problems in the stack

steps.action: On most non-bass synth layers, high-pass / low-cut around below 100 Hz (consistent across layers) so they do not fight the bass.
steps.expect: Synth layers cleaned of unnecessary sub

steps.action: Add bell cuts where layers pile up in the mids; deepen cuts as needed so each hook synth owns different mid space.
For a bright topper layer, consider a committed high-pass (transcript example: cut everything below ~1 kHz) so it supplies air/presence while lower layers own body.
steps.expect: Topper sits above without adding mud

steps.action: If a layer is harsh/tenny, pull offending upper bands by ear (not only by analyzer). Re-check in full mix with bass/kick.

verification: Harsh highs eased; stack clearer in context
